title: Circus Panda
text: “So, whaddya want me to do, exactly?” Panda asked Father sulkily after taking a swig of booze.
“There’s a circus running over in Melromarc. Your job would basically be to help out by literally drawing in customers, I guess?”
“Aside from that, guarding Father, indeed. You must protect him thoroughly, and also tend to his needs at night, I say.”
“Motoyasu-kun! You’re still going on about that!?”

Father scolded me, but this was an important matter, I say. Now, was that so? In my case, I’d often been introduced to a wealthy household’s parents and relatives when brought along for a meeting. Of course, there were times things went against me, but there were also occasions where, having already gotten acquainted with the parents through some prior event and earned their favor, I was granted grand permission to pursue the relationship. Well, whether things would actually progress from there to the end was always uncertain. Since I’d already grown close with both the father and grandfather here, I figured the obstacles would be relatively few, indeed.
“Hahaha, if you two hit it off, I’d be happy for you two to get along. In fact, I’d be glad if you’d take care of this kid, if you don’t mind.”
“Don’t go deciding things on your own!”
Bam! Panda slammed the table.
“Well, why don’t you talk it over a bit before deciding? There’s plenty of time.”
“Geez, why’s this turning into some kind of matchmaking session…”
“Ah… true, it is starting to feel that way. In this case, does that make Motoyasu-kun my go-between?”
“Indeed it does. I shall see to it that the match proceeds smoothly, I say.”
“I said don’t decide things on your own!”

Hmm… Panda really was stubborn, in her own way. In the previous loop, she’d ended up quite thoroughly attached to Father, so there shouldn’t be an issue here. It seemed Panda’s type happened to be Father. When thoroughly drunk, she’d let slip her true feelings and gushed about him plenty, so there was no mistaking it. Curious, I tried to dig deeper into my memories. As for why Panda was drawn to Father… it seemed to have something to do with the fact that Father carried a certain atmosphere similar to the father of Tiger Girl and the others—her first love. In other words, her first impression of him had apparently been quite favorable from the start. More than anything, once Father actually got to know Panda, the two of them generally seemed to get along. Even when teased, she’d get angry, sure, but it never crossed into outright dislike. Well, personally, I’d like Father to graduate from his virginity sooner rather than later. Father was awfully reserved about that sort of thing, after all. I’d figured he and Older Sister might end up together fairly early on, but this time around, things weren’t going well on that front. Ugh… Rival could show up at any moment, so I needed to find some way to speed things along and establish a reliable pattern. The fastest case in my memory was probably the loop where I failed to save Father from the false accusation, and he ended up meeting Older Sister early on. Any other route, and things dragged out uncomfortably late. Perhaps that was the way to go, then? Feign the role of an experienced older brother brimming with curiosity about such things, casually mention a place I knew well, introduce Father to a lady of the establishment, and pay the bill… Given his interest, I felt confident Father would go through with the experience without much trouble.
“Father, since Panda doesn’t seem too eager, shall we head out to the pleasure district tonight?”
“Motoyasu-kun? What exactly are you planning to make me do by taking me to a place like that?”
“Why, having a professional in that particular field see to Father’s graduation from virginity, of course. A hero must have experience, after all, I say.”
“Even for you, that’s a bit too much of a fastball to throw at me out of nowhere. I’ll have to pass on that one, thanks.”

Hmm… so at this stage, Father wasn’t interested—no, wait, he was interested, but his motivation was thin. It seemed he really did want his first experience to be with someone he’d grown close to. Rather frustrating, I must say.
“Why the heck are you two getting along with a guy like this?”
Panda held her head in her hands, glancing back and forth between her adoptive father and grandfather.
“Sure, he’s got a few issues, but there’s no malice in him.”
“Strength surpasses all else.”
Her adoptive father and grandfather brushed off Panda’s complaint without hesitation.
“More than anything, Shield Hero-sama has a moral compass. Larsa, he thought up a meal plan with your health in mind together with me, so let’s all eat together later.”
“The flavor’s guaranteed. I was practically playing around perfecting it to my own taste.”
“Sigh…”
“By the way, his tolerance for alcohol is considerable. No matter what happens, you’ll never beat him, so brace yourself.”
“Yeah, yeah.”

And so Panda chatted idly with her family while sneaking glances at Father now and then. Honestly—not that I’m one to talk—but this Panda sure looked at Father a lot for a first meeting. Even at their very first encounter, she’d reacted almost instantly the moment Father pointed at her. Would someone really care that much just from being pointed at by some random bystander? In that sense, perhaps she’d already sensed something about Father from the start.
“Geez, Elmelo…”
“Like I said before, right? You’ll come out with fewer scars if you just go along with it quietly here.”
Elephant, playing the part of mediator, was fielding Panda’s complaints while attending to Kou and Filo-tan at the same time.
“I swear I’m getting back at you for this someday.”
“Don’t worry. In the near future, I’m guaranteed to get dragged into something similarly ridiculous myself…”
Watching Elephant stare off into the distance, Panda furrowed her brow as if she’d sensed something.
“Just what kind of weakness does he have on you, exactly…”
“Well… Motoyasu-kun seems to know an awful lot about things… regarding Elmelo-san’s family home…”
“How much exactly. Actually, more importantly, how the heck did you even find out in the first place?”
“I’ve been looping, indeed.”
And so it was decided that Panda would be given a rough explanation about the loops. In any case, this was how Panda ended up employed as the circus’s crowd-drawing panda.

It seemed Panda had taken over the job her grandfather used to do, becoming a clown—a proper Crown. When it came to the makeup, they went for quite a punk-style decoration, and it seemed Panda rather liked this particular style, since she went along with it eagerly.
“Something like this, then?”
She’d turned the dark patches around her eyes into stars. Below them, in proper clown fashion, she’d also drawn on tears.
“Ah, that actually looks pretty cool. Though personally, I’m fine with the plain, natural Larsa-san too.”
“D-Don’t go saying embarrassing things like that!”
Panda shouted at Father, her face flushing red.
“So, at the entrance it’s ball-balancing followed by juggling… geez, I really wish I could skip this acrobatics nonsense.”
Grumbling all the while, Panda flawlessly began balancing on the ball regardless.
“Ooh! Amazing, amazing! You’re really good at this.”
“This much is nothing, indeed.”

This Panda really was quite the skilled performer. I’d bet she could probably manage tightrope walking on a unicycle too, if it came to that. Well, her grandfather often did tightrope acts too—performing dances while holding a pole.
“I have to say, Larsa-san, you really are skilled. I can see why Motoyasu-kun was so eager to recruit you.”

She was also skilled with knife-throwing, and in that department, Panda outperformed even her grandfather during the show. Her subordinates were doing things like jumping through rings of fire. The lineup of acts felt like it kept growing larger by the day. Incidentally, Elephant ended up turning completely white all over at one point—covered in flour, if I recalled correctly. It seemed only a matter of time before my own Drive Mode got its big debut too. As for another interesting side discovery—once Father, Panda, and Panda’s adoptive father all joined the circus together, the three of them seemed to end up cooking together quite often.
“Sending ingredients your way!”
“Same here—catch this in exchange!”
“Thanks!”

Whenever Father and Panda’s adoptive father cooked together in the kitchen, ingredients would go flying through the air, making it impossible for anyone else to step in between them. Ingredients soaring through the air, landing perfectly in the pot. Panda, however, could stroll right into the middle of all that without so much as blinking.
“Just borrowing a bit of this, indeed.”

She’d snag some of the ingredients flying about and stir-fry them up in a wok on the spot. Sure, her cooking skills were a notch below Father and the others, but simply being able to stand within that whirlwind of activity was proof enough of some serious skill.
